title: Regional fleet topology, failback rules, and data locality controls
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity are increasingly asking for stronger regional guarantees: enforceable throughput SLAs for a region, clear automatic behavior when a zone becomes unhealthy, and guaranteed data residency for request payloads and logs. This ticket defines the product requirements and operational playbook for regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets focusing on placement topology, automated failback (not just failover), and data locality controls.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Product: UI + API to create a Regional Dedicated Fleet that pins resource placement to a region and specifies allowed zones and preferred failover order
2) SLA: Documented per-region throughput guarantee semantics (credits, throttling, & grace period) and enforcement behavior during partial outage

3) Autoscale: Autoscale policy types exposed: strict-capacity (no cross-region spill), regional-prewarm (maintain warm pool within region), and cost-optimized (allow cross-region fallback with encryption/e2e logging), with defaults and templated policies

4) Data residency: Option on fleet creation to enforce hard residency (no cross-region processing) or soft residency (notify and require approval for cross-region processing). Audit logs must capture any cross-region actions
5) Failback: Automated failback plan that returns traffic to the primary region after health stabilization within configurable windows; ability to opt into manual failback only
6) Ops: Runbook and console page showing current residency state, reason codes for cross-region routing, and one-click rollback to previous placement policy
7) Tests: Integration tests that simulate zone degradation, full region drain, and controlled failback; measure 95/99th percentile token latency under both normal and failover conditions
8) Observability: Console metrics for cross-region egress volume, number of cross-region fallbacks in last 30 days, and SLA credit accounting
engineering_notes: Proposed approach: implement a RegionPlacement policy object for Dedicated fleets. Runtime will evaluate policy at request ingress and consult placement driver. Key implementation pieces owned by ENG: (a) policy schema and API, (b) router enforcement with egress tagging, (c) admission control to verify warm-pool size, and (d) audit/logging hooks. Edge cases: transient partition vs sustained capacity loss; need hysteresis parameters. Dependencies ENG-19234 (regional routing API) and ENG-19801 (warm-pool allocator).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): internal-only Regional fleets with hard residency disabled; test with 2 pilots. Phase 2 (beta): expose residency toggle in console + API; enable audit logs and SLA accounting. Phase 3 (GA): default policy templates, legal/compliance sign-off, and performance SLAs. Rollback: policy change is reversible; fleet can toggle to allow cross-region routing which immediately reduces capacity pressure in origin region.
open_questions: Q1: Should hard residency forbid cross-region caching (KV caches) or only forbid execution outside region?
Q2: What legal/contract language is required to offer 'soft residency' commercial plans?
Q3: How many pre-warmed units are reasonable as default for regional-prewarm vs strict-capacity templates?
Q4: What is acceptable SLA credit formula during partial zone degradations vs full-region loss?
Q5: Operational: who gets paged for automated cross-region failover? (SRE on-call + customer-owned contacts?)
